To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we isolated two new compounds from A. latifolia, which were evaluated for their in vitro cytotoxic activities.
we isolated 13 compounds from Ainsliaeda latifolia, and evaluated their cytotoxic activity against five cancer cell lines.
we have discovered the cytotoxicity of two new compounds including one sesquiterpenoids and one monoterpenoid from the whole plant of Ainsliaela latifolia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical constituents and bioactivity of A. latifolia, which may contribute to the development of new drugs.
the isolation of new natural compounds and the evaluation of their bioactivities.
the isolation, structural elucidation, and biological evaluation of compounds from the whole plants …
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

compounds 1-10 showed no cytotoxicity against five cancer cell lines (A549, MCF-7, HepG2, HeLa, and SMMC-7721), while compounds 2, 4, 5, and 8 exhibited significant cytotoxicity against the SMMC-7722 cell line.
compound 3 showed the most potent cytotoxicity against the four tested tumor cell lines, with the IC50 values of 0.9 μg/mL against MCF-7 and 0.8 μg/mL against A549.
the compounds 1 and 2 showed potent cytotoxic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

compound 1 was the first example of the sesquiterpenoids bearing the unusual 3-epi-cubeban-11-one skeleton, compounds 2, 3 and 6 were the first examples of the monoterpenoid derivatives of 1,8-cineol and 1-phenyl-1,3-butanedione, and compounds 2 and 4 exhibited moderate activities against the tested tumor cell lines.

compound 1 was found to be the most potent cytotoxic agent among all the tested compounds, which exhibited potent cytotoxicity against A549, HepG2, Hela, and SMMC-7721 cell lines with IC50 values of 0.17, 0.17 0.16, and 0.18 μM, respectively.
the sesquiterpenes and monoterpenes are the main constituents of the whole plants of the species A. latifolia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sesquiterpenoids and monoterpene compounds from the plant have significant cytotoxic activities against the tested human cancer cell lines.

the new sesquiterpene, 3,4-dihydro-2,4a-dimethyl-2-(4-methylpent-2-enyl)-2H-pyran-6-carboxylic acid (3), exhibited significant cytotoxicity against human lung cancer cell line (A549) with an IC50 value of 0.7 μM.
the cytotoxic activity of the compounds is related to the presence of an α,β-unsaturated lactone moiety in the structure.
